etymology: From the marksman who fires into a barn and then paints the target around the tightest cluster.
committed_when: A large dataset is available and a story is wanted.
tell: The hypothesis was formed after the data was seen, and this is not mentioned.
counter: Ask what the prediction was before the data arrived, and what the same measure shows in the cases not chosen.
senses: Finding a pattern in data after the fact, then presenting the pattern as though it had been predicted.
It works because a cluster really is a cluster. With enough data, some grouping will be tight; the fallacy is the order of operations, which nobody can see in the finished result.
example: *“Crimes cluster around these three blocks.”* So does every address in the city, when you draw the box around three blocks.

confused_with.tell: The sharpshooter keeps all the data and moves the target; the cherry picker keeps the target and drops the data.
